author: Miriam Fabrycky
title: Celebrate USA 250 with unique events around Bucks County, Philadelphia - NewsBreak
text:
By Miriam Fabrycky ,
1 days ago From fireworks to parades , there’s no shortage of classic Independence Day events in Bucks County.
But there are also plenty of alternative options for anyone seeking a celebration off the beaten path.
Here are some unique USA 250 experiences from around the Philadelphia region.
Discover Pennsylvania artists with a statewide scavenger hunt In honor of Pennsylvania's role in securing American liberty, America250PA is displaying more than 120 fiberglass bells throughout the commonwealth. There's at least one bell in each Pennsylvania counties, all designed by local artists.
Bucks County's bell is titled "Local Color" and was designed by artist James Feehan. It's displayed inside the ShopRite in Yardley.
Bucks' bordering counties host even more liberty bells. Northampton and Lehigh are each displaying one, Montgomery sports two, and Philadelphia boasts no fewer than 26 scattered throughout the city — perfect for a summer scavenger hunt.
An interactive map of the art trail, along with information regarding each of the individual bells, may be viewed on Pennsylvania's tourism website .
Reimagine Washington's Crossing at the Michener Art Museum Michener Art Museum in Doylestown welcomes visitors to reflect on public memory and our national mythology in a new exhibition featuring artistic responses to Emmanual Leutze's famous painting, "Washington Crossing the Delaware."
"The Crossing: Picturing the American Revolution" exhibits pieces by notable national and international artists. Highlights include the first museum display of acclaimed contemporary artist and Chinese dissident Ai Weiwei's large toy brick reproduction of Leutze's painting, along with a three-dimensional "found object" reconstruction of Washington's Crossing by Pennsylvania artist Vanessa German.
Works by past and contemporary artists including Robert Beck, Charles W. Hargens, Edward Hicks, Mort Künstler, Kent Monkman and William Francis Taylor round out the exhibition, offering thought-provoking interpretations of one of Bucks County's best-known historical events.
“The contemporary work included in The Crossing memorializes and responds to the past and also elicits dialogue and imagines new futures for the United States,” said Laura Turner Igoe, Gerry and Marguerite Lenfest chief curator at Michener Art Museum. “These artists encourage us to tell our own stories on a monumental scale.”
Opening hours and ticket information are available on the Michener Art Museum website .
Indulge in "LiberTea" or a "Colonial Calm Spa" at the Rittenhouse Hotel This summer, a five-star Philadelphia hotel is offering two luxurious America250-themed experiences.
The Rittenhouse Hotel's Mary Cassatt Tea Room is hosting afternoon teas inspired by the gatherings organized by Patriot women during the tea boycotts. In-house-made tea blends, pastries and cocktails feature patriotic names, colors and flavors. Reservations are required for "LiberTea," priced at $70 per person.
The Rittenhouse Spa & Club is also offering a "Colonial Calm Spa Ritual" including a signature massage with native botanical products. Pricing starts at $215 for 50 minutes and $255 for 80 minutes.
Polish heritage at the National Shrine of Our lady of Czestochowa Many Americans know the Revolutionary War history of European nations such as France and Spain, but may be less familiar with Poland’s contributions to American independence. A Doylestown shrine Lyndon B. Johnson once described as “a monument to freedom” aims to address that historical gap.
The National Shrine of Our Lady of Czestochowa features dozens of stained glass panels tracing the intersecting histories of America, Poland and Catholicism. The panels include depictions of famed war hero Casimir Pulaski, the “Father of the American Calvary,” with George Washington, and of military architect Tadeusz Kościuszko, who designed West Point’s fortifications, with Thomas Jefferson.
The National Shrine is a short drive from Moland House in Warminster, where Washington first met Pulaski.
The community is currently observing a week of prayer in anticipation of America’s 250th anniversary.
“All are welcome,” said the Rev. Krzystof Wieliczko in an announcement . Opening hours are listed online .
Tour Doylestown Cemetery on Friday, July 3 at 7:30 p.m. While most America250 celebrations focus on the beginning of our nation's history, we wouldn't be celebrating the semiquincentennial if it weren't for those who fought to keep our Union together. Learn more about the locals who gave their lives for the Union at a special tour of Doylestown Cemetery with the Bucks County Civil War Museum.
The tour begins at the Caretaker's House on the corner of Spruce and Court Streets in Doylestown. Tickets are $10, and children younger than 16 may attend for free.
Revolutionary history at Washington Crossing, Saturday, July 4 Rain or shine, the historic town of Washington Crossing is to see its 44th Annual RevRun on Independence Day.
The 1-mile fun run begins at 8 a.m., while the Certified 5k Race and Certified 10k Race are to begin respectively at 8:15 and 8:45 a.m.
Participants may register in-person on the day of the race or online . Those who register online by July 3 are guaranteed a commemorative T-shirt. Proceeds support emergency services, scholarships and historic preservation in Upper Makefield Township.
'Float your wish' on Saturday, July 4 from 1-3 p.m. Have a wish for "Yardley, America, the Earth, the Universe or you" ? Write it on a rubber duck and send it sailing out into Lake Afton.
The Yardley Historical Association is providing 103 rubber ducks, markers and paper at this free July 4 event. A canoeist is to collect the ducks later in the afternoon and return them to any participants who wish to keep their wishes.
Butterfly House on Sunday, July 5, 11 a.m. to 3 p.m. Churchville Nature Center is kicking off its 2026 season with a special semiquincentennial discount. For one day only, tickets to the Butterfly House are to be reduced to $2.50. Members and children ages 3 and younger may enter free.
Zoom in on history at the Morris Arboretum Garden Railway A Philadelphia favorite is getting a Revolutionary refresh this summer. The miniature railway at the Morris Arboretum and Garden is to wind through a model city inspired by colonial-era Philadelphia and constructed with exclusively organic material.
Featuring replicas of Independence Hall, the Battle of Germantown and other historic landmarks along over a third of a mile of track, the railway is designed to delight visitors of all ages.
Hours and pricing are available on the Morris Arboretum and Garden's website .
